description.value: Copper Beech House is a heritage inn in Masset on the north coast of Haida Gwaii, set in a historic 1914 house overlooking Delkatla Inlet and managed by Canadian poet and writer Susan Musgrave. The property is celebrated for its eccentric literary character—walls hung with Haida art and bookshelves stocked by celebrated guests including Margaret Atwood, David Suzuki, and Douglas Coupland. It has been featured in Vogue and National Geographic, making it one of the most distinctive and storied places to stay in remote British Columbia.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is live, active (copyright 2026), and describes the property as open year-round. A critical contact discrepancy exists: OSM lists +1 250 626 5441 but the website consistently shows +1 (250) 626-9666 on every page, and the street suffix differs (OSM: 'Delkatla Street' vs website: 'Delkatla Rd'). Cyclist use is confirmed by a guest review stating 'After riding our bikes all day and returning in the afternoon…', but no website content addresses bike storage, bike procedures, laundry, Wi-Fi, or other cycling-specific amenities.
concerns: Phone number mismatch: OSM lists +1 250 626 5441 but website consistently shows +1 (250) 626-9666 across all pages — OSM number appears outdated.
Street name discrepancy: OSM records 'Delkatla Street' but website contact footer shows '1590 Delkatla Rd, Masset, BC V0T 1M0'.
Name discrepancy: OSM lists 'Copper Beech Guest House' but the website uses 'Copper Beech House' and 'Copper Beech House Inn' throughout.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a highly notable accommodation in a remote cycle-touring destination (Haida Gwaii) with confirmed cyclist guests, but the website provides no evidence for either required WWC criterion; direct outreach is needed to confirm bike storage and staff bike procedures before listing.
enrichment_extras.notes: A guest review explicitly references cycling ('After riding our bikes all day and returning in the afternoon, Sunnie had put out homemade scones and bananas'), confirming the property regularly hosts cycle-touring guests. The 'Our Services' subpage was listed in site navigation but its full content was not captured in the prefetch; it may contain bike storage or amenity details not visible in the available text.
